concept: To Make a Mixture from Two Mixtures
question: How many kilograms of tea, costing ₹250 per kg must be mixed with 25 kg of tea costing ₹400 per kg so that there may be a profit of 10% on selling the mixture at ₹330 per kg?
solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of first tea = ₹250 per kg

Cost price of second tea = ₹400 per kg

Quantity of second tea = 25 kg

Selling price of the mixture = ₹330 per kg

**Formula used:**

Cost price of mixture = frac{{Selling Price} times 100}{100 + {Profit%}}

Let the required quantity of first tea be x kg.

Average cost price = (x times 250 + 25 times 400)/(x + 25)

**Calculation:**

Cost price of mixture = (330 times 100)/(110)

⇒ Cost price of mixture = ₹300 per kg

⇒ (x times 250 + 25 times 400)/(x + 25) = 300

⇒ 250x + 10000 = 300(x + 25)

⇒ 250x + 10000 = 300x + 7500

⇒ 2500 = 50x

⇒ x = (2500)/(50) = 50

∴ The required quantity of first tea is 50 kg.

cost price of all mixture is (330 × 100)/110

⇒ Rs. 300/- per kg
